area: the web3:// site (Premises/ERC-5219 router), Chrome, Desk* clients, Page* contracts, the /c console (PageConsole, ConsoleRead, ConsoleSkin, engine/console.*), CONSOLE.md, INTERFACE.md, tools/site.mjs, tools/gateway.mjs
summary:
IPSEITY serves an entire web application from contract storage with no server, IPFS or fetch. `Premises.request(string[] resource, KeyValue[] params)` (src/Premises.sol:251) is an ERC-5219 HTTP handler returning (uint16 status, string body, KeyValue[] headers); `resolveMode()` returns the exact word "5219" so any ERC-6860 web3:// client resolves it with no gateway; 20 page contracts are immutable constructor args and compose HTML in view functions, while the browser JavaScript ships as Solidity string constants in the Desk* contracts or as frozen SSTORE2 data contracts (two ConsoleSkin instances holding console.css and console.js+console-lanes.js). The artwork routes (/, /token/<id>/raw|live|face/<n>|sigil.svg) are answered by Premises directly from the hub and renderer and never pass through a page — that split is the stated safety argument (a compromised router can frame but not alter the artwork). Every response carries Cache-Control (15 s pages, 86,400 s 301s), bad paths are 404 documents never reverts, and one resource has exactly one URL. An HTTP gateway (tools/gateway.mjs) is a pure convenience: each GET is one eth_call of request(); ENS reaches the contract through the ERC-6821 contentcontract record served by Nameplate.

Ownership gating: reading is never gated anywhere (the contract cannot know the caller; the page's msg.sender is Premises). In the browser, Chrome.WALLET_JS collects EIP-6963 announcers (chosen, never raced; remembered in localStorage 'ipse.wallet'), Desk.CORE_JS connects via eth_requestAccounts and refuses a wrong chain before any read that determines a transaction, and the clients learn which tokens are yours by calling the hub's balanceOf then walking tokenOfOwnerByIndex (cap 64) — no list, no signature challenge, no session. The chat/terminal set a speaking token (`ME`, localStorage 'ipse.me') and toggle body.held so .gate (connect card) hides and .only (composers) show; the console server-renders ownerOf into the crest/seed, rewrites HELD to 'you' when eth_accounts[0] matches, and `onlyHolder()` withholds holder-only controls for strangers. Holder controls are deliberately shown to everyone and refused by the chain: the hub's onlyOwner(id) admits the ERC-721 owner or the token's own ERC-6551 Reach; Parley.mayActAs is owner-or-Reach (not the renter); Lease/Consign/Succession take strict-owner doors; session keys are checked by sessionAllows on every call, and /k/<id>/<key> only sends executeAsSession from the key's own wallet.

Client discipline (enforced by tools/verify-site.mjs, 586 assertions at last run, and tools/verify-console.mjs, 58): every 4-byte selector is keccak'd on chain by the contract that serves the page and shipped in a JSON config block written with Web.jsonEsc (so a `</script>` symbol cannot end it); the browser ships no keccak and no ABI coder (four small hand encoders are each proven against a contract that does hash); all amounts are BigInt; every chain string reaches the DOM through textContent; Web.esc is a printable-ASCII whitelist; every satellite read is try/catch plus extcodesize so a chain missing a pool or lease degrades a section instead of reverting the page; 'zero' and 'not reported' are different facts (ConsoleRead.reported bitmask). Unique surfaces: the per-token console at /c/<id>[/verb] (seven plain-English verbs, the token's own hue in :root before any script, a depth-walk drawn as 1px margin rules carried in the URL fragment, a confirm slab before every send that then follows the receipt), a terminal that is one code path for people and agents (TERM.run(line), TERM.commands() as data, 46 words registered from three contracts), an indexer-free chat client that walks Parley's back-pointers one eth_getLogs block at a time with sealed DMs from a wallet-signature-derived P-256 key, a machine-readable shopfront ipseity.services/2 with selectors and a session-key service, a launchpad whose CREATE2 hook salt is mined by eth_call, and /hook/<addr> reading v4 permissions off address bits with no call.

State of the code: 35 site-only runtime contracts (44 deployed by deploySite in a load-bearing order with a nonce-predicted Nameplate), five of them within 2–6% of EIP-170 (DeskTerm 23,908 B = 97.3%, PageLaunch 23,494, Desk 23,401, Chrome 23,310, PageManifest 23,105); the console shipped as four contracts with raw JS rather than the spec's 14 contracts with gzipped lanes, its TRADE/SPEAK lanes are 'unbuilt' notes on main (filled on the unmerged branch origin/claude/claude-md-docs-8vvyc8), no 302 redirects retire the 19 flat pages, Chrome is 94.8% of the ceiling and still carries CSS for a deleted tesseract, the console and /k use window.ethereum only (not the EIP-6963 chooser), DeskEstate listens for an 'ip:account' event nobody dispatches, and several doc numbers (README size table, test counts, five-chain partition) are stale. Nothing is audited. Live on Ethereum Sepolia (Premises 0x7e1bdcd82e2a1d197f5792ff41e6548e01ad7a31, PageConsole 0x975579ec…) and Base Sepolia (Premises 0xc59f75d2…).

standards_implemented: ERC-6821 contentcontract + ERC-3770 (via Nameplate, explained on /name)
Uniswap v3 (QuoterV2, SwapRouter, SwapRouter02, factory, positions) and v4 (PoolManager.initialize, hook address bits, PositionManager, Permit2)
ENS DNS wire format, ENSIP-10 wildcard, registrar renew
unique_ideas: The website is served by the NFT's own contracts over ERC-5219/web3:// — pages are view functions, JS is contract bytecode or SSTORE2 shards, and the artwork routes never pass through a replaceable page.
resolveMode() = "5219" as the four bytes that make a conformant web3:// client find the site without any gateway.

Every 4-byte selector the browser sends is keccak'd on chain by the contract serving the page and shipped in a jsonEsc'd JSON block; the browser carries no keccak and no ABI coder, and the few hand encoders are proven against contracts that do hash.

The per-token console /c/<id>/<verb>: seven plain-English verbs, the token's hue in :root before any script, server-rendered state so the no-script page is correct, controls that appear once the wallet proves holding, a confirm slab before every send that then follows the receipt.
The depth walk carried in the URL fragment (#w=id:hue,…) and drawn as 1px margin rules — the fragment never reaches ERC-5219, so no contract byte and no cache key.
ConsoleRead's reported bitmask: a clear bit is 'not reported', a set bit with zero is 'none' — plus extcodesize before try/catch because try alone reverts on a codeless address.
A terminal that is an API with a keyboard: TERM.run(line) and TERM.commands() are the same code path for people and agents; words register from companion contracts to dodge EIP-170.
Indexer-free chat: each message carries the block of the previous one, so a client walks history with single-block eth_getLogs and no range scan; token number is identity.
Sealed DMs with a key derived from a wallet signature (nothing stored), recovered via a PKCS#8 import so no curve arithmetic ships; the published point dies with the sale.
services.json/2: a machine-readable shopfront generated from the same reads as the page, with selectors, rent.use powers, and a session-key service plus /k/<id>/<key> as the agent's own door.
Holding verified by enumerating the collection itself (balanceOf + tokenOfOwnerByIndex) — no list, no login; holder controls shown to everyone and refused by the chain.
A CREATE2 hook salt mined by eth_call (Kiln.mine windows) so the browser never needs keccak; /hook/<addr> reads v4 permissions off address bits with no call.
The market picker and token list are derived from the pool that would execute the trade, never fetched from a hosted list.

Hostile-ERC-20 hardening on the rendering path (Web._label: offset must equal 32 before dereference; 30k/50k gas stipends; 32-char labels) after an OffsetBombToken cost 2,151M gas of memory expansion.
A confirm-slab rule with no exception: no path from a text field to a broadcast transaction.
Companion-contract pattern for EIP-170 (DeskRooms/DeskWill via TERM.def, DeskEstate, LaunchView) and a nonce-predicted resolver address asserted at deploy.
weaknesses: Two interfaces coexist: 19 flat routes in Chrome's language and the console; the spec's 302 redirects and Chrome retirement never shipped.

wallet_gating: Reading is never gated (the contract cannot know the caller; a page's msg.sender is Premises). Client side: Chrome.WALLET_JS collects EIP-6963 announcers and chooses one (localStorage 'ipse.wallet'); Desk.CORE_JS connect() = eth_requestAccounts + eth_chainId check against the page's chain; holding is proven by calling the hub's balanceOf(address) and walking tokenOfOwnerByIndex (cap 64) — DeskTalk held(), DeskTerm mine() — then become(id) sets the speaking token (localStorage 'ipse.me') and body.held toggles .gate (connect card hidden) / .only (composers shown). The console server-renders ownerOf into the crest and window.CON.owner, rewrites HELD to 'you' when eth_accounts[0] matches, and onlyHolder() withholds holder-only controls for strangers while the state still renders; /k/<id>/<key> refuses to send unless eth_requestAccounts[0] equals the key. On chain the contracts decide: hub onlyOwner(id) = ERC-721 owner or the token's ERC-6551 Reach (src/Ipseity.sol:291-299); Parley.mayActAs = owner or Reach, not the renter (src/Parley.sol:168-173); Lease/Consign/Succession strict-owner; session keys via sessionAllows on every executeAsSession. Rule stated in INTERFACE.md: reading is never gated and holding is never login; controls are shown and refused by the chain, never hidden. No SIWE, no server session, no signature challenge.
website_delivery: Entirely from chain. Premises.request(string[] resource, KeyValue[] params) (ERC-5219) returns (uint16 status, string body, KeyValue[] headers); resolveMode() returns "5219" so ERC-6860 web3:// clients resolve it natively (web3://<premises>[:chainId]/...). Twenty page contracts (immutable constructor args) compose HTML in view functions from live reads; browser JS ships as Solidity string constants in Desk*.sol (window.IP, window.TERM, window.IPT, window.UNI…) or, for the console, as raw bytes in two frozen SSTORE2 ConsoleSkin stores (console.css; console.js+console-lanes.js) concatenated into the document by PageConsole.doc(). Every page carries a <script type=application/json> config block with addresses and on-chain-hashed selectors. The artwork routes (/, /token/<id>/live|raw|face/<n>|sigil.svg) are answered by Premises from the hub/renderer directly; /live serves Renderer.document() on a real origin so EIP-6963 wallets inject (a data: document has an opaque origin). An HTTP gateway (tools/gateway.mjs; w3link.io publicly) is optional: each GET is one eth_call of request() relaying the contract's status/Content-Type/Cache-Control. ENS names reach the contract via the ERC-6821 contentcontract record served by Nameplate. Measured: /token/1/live 4.48M gas (54,432 B) vs tokenURI 19.99M; flat pages 0.08–0.31M; the still 3.32M. The instrument's own /connect binds a wallet and leaves for /c/<id> (engine/ipseity.html:578, LANDING).
pitfalls: `try` does not survive a codeless address: check extcodesize first (ConsoleRead._live) or the whole page reverts on chains missing a satellite.
An ERC-20 string return must be validated (offset == 32, len ≤ payload) before dereference — an attacker-chosen offset cost 2,151M gas of memory expansion and killed a 24-row directory.
JSON escaping is not HTML escaping: a jsonEsc'd `\u003cscript\u003e` comes back as `<script>` from JSON.parse — scrub symbols again at the one place every ticker passes.
address args are right-aligned, bytes4 args left-aligned; swapping them in grantSession silently grants a selector nobody chose.
Two Uniswap routers share exactInputSingle with structs differing by one field; the wrong shape does not revert, it shifts recipient and amounts — store the router kind beside the address.
QuoterV2's NatSpec parameter order differs from its struct order; hash the declaration.
Zero amountIn on SwapRouter02 is the CONTRACT_BALANCE sentinel, not an empty trade.
A negative tick zero-padded instead of sign-extended mints a position in a range nobody chose — use two's complement words.
A custom property containing var() is substituted where it is declared: re-declare --a on every band or every level is the first token's colour.
pointer-events:none on the standing band makes the console unclickable while every screenshot looks perfect.
A body fade implemented as a class the script adds leaves the server-rendered page invisible when a script throws — use a CSS animation.
Painting lane controls before eth_accounts answers tells a holder to connect while the crest says 'you'.
A payable mint proposed at zero value reverts; no injected wallet reads a price — read price() and attach it, or refuse.
Seventeen flat constructor args, or six reads inside one string.concat, exceed the stack even under viaIR — pass a struct, split into private functions.
A duplicate JSON key is legal and every parser keeps the last one — the manifest silently lost the quote asset to a `quote` call entry.
Variable-length SSTORE2 loads must not sit between a nonce prediction and the contract it predicts.
A load-balanced public RPC answers 0x for a contract that exists on another replica — retry before believing absence (redeploy-site, DEPLOYMENTS).
Source bytes are not runtime bytes: size with the compiler gate, never by reading the file; four site contracts sit at 94–97% of EIP-170.
Two copies of one naming table drift (verbs, door map, bands, routes) — derive one from the other or hold them equal with a test.
Chrome's EIP-6963 chooser is bypassed by the console and /k (window.ethereum only); DeskEstate's 'ip:account' listener has no dispatcher.
Unlimited ERC-20 approvals on the flat cards; the console branch uses exact amounts.
